title: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery: in-product diagnostics for case access, security filters and holds
summary: Hold: the hold-policy automation shown in the controls table reads status but does not retry distribution. The case-access explanation also omits documented alternatives to eDiscovery Manager membership and the administrator exception to case membership. The roadmap facts and supplied rollout windows match, although the windows should remain tentative.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery is gaining self-service diagnostics that highlight common configuration problems and provide guidance.
claims.quote: Self-service diagnostics help identify common issues with case permissions, security filters, and policy status. The experience highlights potential misconfigurations and provides simple guidance to help customers understand and resolve them.

claims.claim: Microsoft is introducing three diagnostic checks.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery is introducing three read-only diagnostic checks for case access, security filters, and hold-policy distribution.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; summary; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because Microsoft has not published a license requirement for these diagnostics.
claims.quote: Both admins and users working with eDiscovery cases require a Microsoft 365 Enterprise E3 or E5 license.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/edisc-get-started. Replace the licensing explanation with 'Microsoft documents Microsoft 365 Enterprise E3 or E5 licensing for admins and users working with eDiscovery cases. A requirement specific to these diagnostics is not yet published.' Keep the low cost rating and narrow the summary, Open questions and cost rationale to feature-specific licensing.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Neither the roadmap record nor MC1515937 names a license, add-on or consumption charge for the diagnostics.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery is introducing three read-only diagnostic checks for case access, security filters, and hold-policy distribution.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a price specific to these diagnostics.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery diagnostics licensing price; Purview eDiscovery licensing requirements Standard premium diagnostics license. Read edisc-billing, edisc-get-started and edisc-features-components; none prices the three diagnostics.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a meter specific to these diagnostics.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery diagnostics licensing price; Purview eDiscovery licensing requirements Standard premium diagnostics license. Read edisc-billing: meters cover specified storage and Graph export usage, not these diagnostic checks.

claims.claim: The permissions page says a user whose data is analyzed with premium eDiscovery features needs Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5.
claims.quote: To analyze a user's data when premium eDiscovery features are enabled, the user must be assigned an Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5 license.

claims.claim: The permissions page gives Microsoft Purview Suite or Microsoft 365 eDiscovery and Audit add-ons as alternatives for eligible E1 or E3 users.
claims.quote: Alternatively, users with an Office 365 E1 or an Office 365 or Microsoft 365 E3 license can be assigned a Microsoft Purview Suite (formerly known as Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance) or Microsoft 365 eDiscovery and Audit add-on license.

claims.claim: The cited permissions and case-access pages do not specifically describe the three new diagnostics or their license rule.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery in-product diagnostics; eDiscovery diagnostics case access; eDiscovery diagnostics licensing price. Read edisc-permissions and edisc-settings-access-permissions in full: permissions describes the older RBAC diagnostic, not these three checks.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: role group row
claims.claim: Role group assignments are managed at Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Role groups > eDiscovery Manager > Edit.
claims.quote: Go to Settings > Role groups. On Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions, select eDiscovery Manager. On the eDiscovery Manager pane ... Select Edit. On Manage eDiscovery Manager, select Choose users or Choose groups.
claims.fix: The path stops early on the correct item. For manager assignment, use 'Settings > Role groups > eDiscovery Manager > Edit > Manage eDiscovery Manager > Choose users or Choose groups' as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/edisc-permissions.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: role group row
claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember "eDiscoveryManager" -Member <name of security group> adds a security group to the eDiscovery Managers subgroup.
claims.quote: You can add a mail-enabled security group as a member of the eDiscovery Managers subgroup ... Add-RoleGroupMember "eDiscoveryManager" -Member <name of security group>

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: role group row
claims.claim: Assigning eDiscovery permissions requires Organization Management membership or the Role Management role.
claims.quote: You need to be a member of the Organization Management role group or be assigned the Role Management role to assign eDiscovery permissions in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: The table contains existing case-access, search-scoping and hold-distribution controls, rather than settings that configure the new diagnostics.
claims.quote: The diagnostics provide guidance without changing your organization's existing configuration.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls: case membership row
claims.claim: Users can be added through Microsoft Purview portal > eDiscovery > Cases > case > Case settings > Access and permissions > Users > Add.
claims.quote: Select the eDiscovery solution card and then select Cases ... Select a case, then select Case settings ... select Access and permissions. Under Users, select Add to add users to the case.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: case membership row
claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/cases/ediscoveryCases/{ediscoveryCaseId}/caseMembers adds a user or role group to a case.
claims.quote: Add an ediscoveryCaseMember to an ediscoveryCase. The ediscoveryCaseMember can be one of two types: a user or a role group. POST /security/cases/ediscoveryCases/{ediscoveryCaseId}/caseMembers
claims.fix: Keep the endpoint. Add to the row note: 'The request body sets recipientType and identifies the member using id, displayName for a role group, or smtpAddress for a user.' The cited v1.0 reference documents these properties.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed that the new case-access check reads the case membership setting.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery diagnostics case access; eDiscovery in-product diagnostics role data disable. Read edisc-settings-access-permissions, edisc-permissions and purview-compliance-diagnostics; no statement identifies the membership setting as an input to the new check.

claims.claim: No portal path is documented for configuring search permissions filters.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview eDiscovery search permissions filters portal UI configure. Read edisc-search-permission-filtering, including its creation, viewing and modification sections; it documents Security & Compliance PowerShell cmdlets, not a filter-configuration portal path.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls: search permissions filter row
claims.claim: New-ComplianceSecurityFilter -FilterName <name of filter> -Users <user or role group> -Filters <filter> creates a search permissions filter.
claims.quote: Use the New-ComplianceSecurityFilter cmdlet to create a search permissions filter. Here's the basic syntax for this cmdlet: New-ComplianceSecurityFilter -FilterName <name of filter> -Users <user or role group> -Filters <filter>

claims.claim: Running the compliance security filter cmdlets requires Organization Management role group membership.
claims.quote: To run the compliance security filter cmdlets, you need to be a member of the Organization Management role group and have the eDiscovery administrator role assigned in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Running the compliance security filter cmdlets also requires the eDiscovery administrator role.
claims.quote: To run the compliance security filter cmdlets, you need to be a member of the Organization Management role group and have the eDiscovery administrator role assigned in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Using search permissions filter cmdlets requires connections to both Exchange Online and Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: You need to connect to both Exchange Online and Security & Compliance PowerShell to use the compliance security filter cmdlets.

claims.claim: Search permissions filter cmdlets are provided through Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: The following four cmdlets in Security & Compliance PowerShell let you configure and manage search permissions filters: New-ComplianceSecurityFilter; Get-ComplianceSecurityFilter; Set-ComplianceSecurityFilter; Remove-ComplianceSecurityFilter.

claims.where: controls[3].ui; Governance controls: hold distribution row; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: A hold policy can be retried at Microsoft Purview portal > eDiscovery > Cases > case > Hold policies > hold policy > Policy actions > Retry policy.
claims.quote: Select the eDiscovery solution card, then select Cases ... Select a case, then select the Hold policies tab ... select the hold policy you want to retry ... select Policy actions > Retry policy.

claims.where: controls[3].api; Governance controls: hold distribution row
claims.claim: Get-CaseHoldPolicy -Identity <policyname> -DistributionDetail is the automation counterpart for the row's hold-policy status and retry control.
claims.quote: Use the Get-CaseHoldPolicy to view existing case hold policies in the Microsoft Purview compliance portal. To get relevant information about how the hold was applied and the affected locations, you need to include the DistributionDetail switch.
claims.fix: Replace controls[3].api.call and the rendered call with 'Set-CaseHoldPolicy -Identity <policyname> -RetryDistribution'. The existing cited troubleshooting page documents this retry operation, so retain that docs URL. In the note, keep 'Get-CaseHoldPolicy -Identity <policyname> -DistributionDetail' as the separate status-reading command.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Governance controls: hold distribution row
claims.claim: Set-CaseHoldPolicy -RetryDistribution redeploys a hold policy.
claims.quote: Run the Set-CaseHoldPolicy -Identity "policyname" -RetryDistribution to resolve the issue. ... Also in the case hold page in the Microsoft Purview portal, select Retry to redeploy the policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; controls[3].api; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: PowerShell can return hold-policy distribution status and results.
claims.quote: Before contacting Microsoft Support about eDiscovery hold issues, check into what is causing the policy to fail by checking into the DistributionResults, based on the ResultCode: Get-CaseHoldPolicy -Identity "policyname" -DistributionDetail | Select -ExpandProperty DistributionResults

claims.claim: Get-ComplianceSecurityFilter lists existing search permissions filters.
claims.quote: Use Get-ComplianceSecurityFilter to return a list of search permissions filters. Use the FilterName parameter to return information for a specific search filter.

claims.claim: Case access requires membership in the eDiscovery Manager role group.
claims.quote: However, before a user can access an eDiscovery case (and perform tasks in the case), you must add the user to the eDiscovery Manager role group in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.fix: Report the disagreement rather than requiring eDiscovery Manager universally: 'The case-access article says to add users to eDiscovery Manager, while the permissions article also documents eDiscovery permissions through Compliance Administrator, Organization Management and Reviewer role groups.' Cite both https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/edisc-settings-access-permissions and https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/edisc-permissions.

claims.claim: Case membership is required for case access without an administrator exception.
claims.quote: For users who aren't eDiscovery Administrators, the cases shown are limited to those where the user is a member. ... An eDiscovery Administrator can view and access all eDiscovery cases.
claims.fix: Qualify the case-membership premise as 'For users who are not eDiscovery Administrators, case visibility is limited to cases they belong to; an eDiscovery Administrator can view and access all cases.' Use this alongside the corrected permissions statement, citing https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/edisc-permissions.

claims.claim: Search permissions filters govern which mailbox and site content an eDiscovery manager can search.
claims.quote: Use search permissions filtering to let an eDiscovery manager search only a subset of mailboxes and sites in your organization. You can also use permissions filtering to let that same eDiscovery manager search only for mailbox or site content that meets a specific search criteria.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Adding or removing a role in a role group automatically removes that group from every eDiscovery case of which it is a member.
claims.quote: If you add or remove a role from a role group that you added as a member of a case, the role group is automatically removed as a member of the case (or any case the role group is a member of).

claims.where: Governance controls; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The existing eDiscovery RBAC diagnostic is reached through Help > Diag:edisRBACdiag in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Select the Help control in the top right of the Microsoft Purview portal. Enter Diag:edisRBACdiag in search ... to run the eDiscovery RBAC Check test.
claims.fix: Replace the parenthesis with '(Help > Ask a question > search for Diag:edisRBACdiag; the permissions article abbreviates this to Help search)' and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/troubleshoot/microsoft-365/purview/diagnostics/purview-compliance-diagnostics, which explicitly includes Ask a question.

claims.claim: The existing RBAC diagnostic checks whether Search, Export or Preview roles are assigned to a named user.
claims.quote: Run the following diagnostic test to check if the Export, Preview, or Search roles are assigned to the designated admin account. ... In the Run diagnostics section, enter the UPN or email address of the user trying to run an export, preview, or search task.

claims.claim: The notice mentions no automatic remediation; configuration fixes remain separate from the read-only checks.
claims.quote: Admins can use three read-only diagnostics ... The diagnostics provide guidance without changing your organization's existing configuration.

claims.where: front matter: action; Why it matters
claims.claim: The prepare action rating fits a new read-only capability whose existing-behavior changes and enablement default are unstated.
claims.quote: action: "prepare"; summary: "three read-only diagnostic checks"; defaultState: "unknown". The standard assigns review to a new capability with an unstated default when no source says existing behaviour will change.
claims.fix: Set action to review. Keep workflow and runbook preparation as optional advice rather than a decision required before rollout.

claims.claim: The new checks will sit alongside the existing RBAC diagnostic, PowerShell hold distribution results and Retry policy action.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery in-product diagnostics; eDiscovery three read-only diagnostics case access security filters hold distribution. Read edisc-permissions, edisc-hold-manage, resolve-ediscovery-hold-issues and purview-compliance-diagnostics; no statement of future coexistence.
claims.fix: Replace 'The new checks will sit alongside existing troubleshooting routes:' with 'Existing troubleshooting routes include'. Keep the verified list of existing routes without promising how the new checks will coexist with them.
